ok, I just edited this to make sure my question was clear and just thought of this. My question is: You see price moving up and up. Along the way there are many RBR's. Any one of those could be the FL. So to tell which one will be the FL do you look to see which one sits above past resistance? Or do you wait for one of the RBR's to get pulled back to and tested? This way you will see which one will hold and that tells you the right FL. Then when price returns to that test (which will actually be the second return) that is your FTB? Make sense?

ممنون از جوابت Harry! برای شفافیت دربارهٔ چارت‌هایت، آیا FL باید تست شود تا FL شود؟ به چارت‌های زیر نگاه کن. پیکان بنفش به FL اشاره می‌کند. آیا آن را FL می‌نامی به‌خاطر حمایتی که در پیکان‌های زرد نشان داده شد؟ به بیان دیگر آیا حدس می‌زدی که سطحِ پیکان بنفش به‌عنوان FL دوام می‌آورد؟ یا مثل چارت دومِ پایین؟

باشه، همین‌الان پست را ویرایش کردم تا مطمئن شوم سؤالم روشن است و تازه به این فکر افتادم. سؤالم این است: قیمت را می‌بینی که بالا و بالاتر می‌رود. در مسیر، RBR‌های زیادی هست. هرکدام می‌توانند FL باشند. پس برای فهمیدن اینکه کدام FL خواهد بود، نگاه می‌کنی کدام بالای مقاومت گذشته است؟ یا منتظر می‌مانی یکی از RBR‌ها به آن برگردد و تست شود؟ این‌طوری می‌بینی کدام دوام می‌آورد و FL درست را به تو می‌گوید. بعد وقتی قیمت به آن تست برمی‌گردد (که در واقع دومین بازگشت است) همان FTB توست؟ منطقی است؟

این چارت یک FL را نشان می‌دهد که قبلاً علامت زده بودم. آیا FL‌ی که پیکان زرد به آن اشاره می‌کند توسط عرضه قبلی از پیکان آبی ساخته شده بود؟

Hotochin wrote: Thanks for your replies Harry! For clarification though over your charts, does the FL have to be tested to make it the FL? Look at the charts below. The purple arrow is pointing to the FL. Would you call that the FL because of the support that was shown at the yellow arrows? In other words would have you tried and guessed that the level with the purple arrow was going to hold as a FL. Or is it like in chart two below?

ok, I just edited this to make sure my question was clear and just thought of this. My question is: You see price moving up and up. Along the way there are many RBR's. Any one of those could be the FL. So to tell which one will be the FL do you look to see which one sits above past resistance? Or do you wait for one of the RBR's to get pulled back to and tested? This way you will see which one will hold and that tells you the right FL. Then when price returns to that test (which will actually be the second return) that is your FTB? Make sense? /chart

This chart shows my FL I marked from earlier. Was the FL that the yellow arrow is pointing to made by the previous supply from the blue arrow? /chart

Thanks,

hello H, i agree with ttfreitas, we shouldnt bang much about on a flag that aint worth banging. we better look for clear examples rather than trying to curve fit it.

about your questions above. 1) does the FL have to be tested to make it the FL? no it doesnt, your first test of it would be the FTB (that you want to trade). 2) Along the way there are many RBR's. Any one of those could be the FL. So to tell which one will be the FL do you look to see which one sits above past resistance? i wouldnt use any other rule that pick the one that better fits the eye, as you said the best will be those that brake past resistance
